We've partnered with @Microsoft to bring Hermes Agent to the enterprise.

Hermes Enterprise now works inside Microsoft Teams, the Microsoft Store and Azure. In Teams, employees hand Hermes work like financial analysis, document drafts or inbox triage, and review the result in the same chat. Agent workloads run in isolated Azure Container Apps sandboxes.

When someone finds a good way to do a recurring task, Hermes saves it as a skill. With Collective Wisdom, they can share that skill with their team after review, so the next person starts out with the best approach anyone has found to accomplish that task. The skills then grow along with the company.

Companies with strict data residency or procurement rules can run Hermes Enterprise in their own Azure tenant. Our CTO Jeffrey Quesnelle presents how Hermes uses these sandboxes at Microsoft Ignite today, in session BRK448.

Thanks to @M12vc and the @Azure Container Apps team.

Jensen Huang’s resignation has put a spotlight on a big question: how are advanced Nvidia chips reaching China despite US export controls?

Epoch AI senior researcher Isabel Juniewicz found one clue while investigating global AI trade. Trade records are consistent with more than $3 billion of chips smuggled into China via Malaysia.

Between April 2024 and June 2025, China recorded $3.75 billion in server imports from Malaysia. However, Malaysia recorded only $0.6 billion in server exports to China.

For context, a server is a computer that goes in a data center. When servers containing AI chips cross borders, customs records them in the same category as ordinary servers.

Malaysia and China each counted about 36,000 servers shipped in that period.

But Malaysia’s records show about $17,000 per server, while China’s show about $106,000 per server. China’s per-server number is far higher than the cost of non-AI servers, which suggests the imports included AI servers.

Wrapped Monero token XMR1 crashes 99% after issuer-linked wallet sells $13.5M –
Link
XMR1, a wrapped Monero token issued by swap service Wagyu and traded on Hyperliquid’s order book, fell from about $488 to $1 in roughly 30 minutes. A wallet funded by the token’s creator address had received 5.2M XMR1 and sold about $13.5M worth. It is still unclear whether the transfers were authorized or the result of compromised credentials. Native Monero and Hyperliquid’s XMR perps were unaffected and kept trading near $482.
Wrapped assets carry the issuer’s risk. When redemption depends on a single bridge operator, one compromised key can wipe out the peg in minutes.
